items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: The interviewee mentions Ellington only in the context of Barney Bigard's career ('he just played with Ellington because Ellington had hired him'), with no personal interaction or direct relationship described between William Russell and Duke Ellington.

ctx.x: Yeah. But they'd gone together... Anyway, say, 10 years or so ago, quite a while back. Anyway, George Barquet's brother, Sheil, who wasn't as well-known as George, down here at least, had passed for white for years. I know Mineta says he met him once on Canal Street after he started passing, and he said, well, I like it better. I forget. I have that in some of the Mineta interviews. Some of that stuff I'll copy, too, later on, which is on tape. He likes it better. Mineta sort of, you know, he wasn't mad at him or…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: INTERVIEWEE: He'd been with Ellington, I think, at that period, probably.

ctx.x: but I don't know who did he see in New York

do you remember oh everybody from Fats Waller of course was one of his big favorites too there's several pictures taken of him listening to Fats Waller I know and there's a picture I just got the other day I got Eddie Condon's scrapbook there's a picture of him sitting there with somebody was it like Duke Ellington or somebody I believe at some club listening to Mez and other people I don't know how they all got together that way but anyway Mez Mesro was one of his favorites he lived up in Harlem with Mez Mez was…

noticed it myself speaking about Eddie Condon did did did did Eddie Condon to your knowledge fulfill a kind of communal role for the musicians that outside of you know that set as a replacement for any of the New Orleans musicians did the New Orleans musicians associate with him at all
